findings.title: `prisma` is used without being imported
findings.body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module has no `@calcom/prisma` import. Type-checking fails with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`, preventing the app-store package from building.

findings.title: Google refresh persists the Zod safe-parse wrapper as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call which returned the credential object itself. This update stores that wrapper in `Credential.key`; on the next request `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives no top-level token fields and rejects the saved Google credential, breaking the integration after its first refresh.

findings.title: The sync token schema strips expiry and provider token fields
findings.body: The computed keys are literal `"[object Object]"` property names, not catch-all/index signatures; the second one also overwrites the first. Zod objects strip unknown fields by default, so in sync mode parsing a normal response returns only `access_token`, then line 26 adds a synthetic `refresh_token`. Expiry values, real refresh tokens, scopes, and provider-specific fields are discarded before callers persist them, producing unusable credentials (for example Zoom computes an invalid expiry and Google loses its stored refresh token).

findings.title: Sync mode changes refresh results into an incompatible response type
findings.body: The sync branch always returns the native Fetch `Response`, while several supplied refresh functions return an SDK response or a token object and their callers continue to consume those shapes. Google reads `res.data`, HubSpot reads `expiresIn`/`accessToken` directly, and the Zoho integrations read Axios `tokenInfo.data`; none of these callers parses the Fetch response body. Enabling `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` therefore causes undefined-token errors or writes invalid credentials for these integrations.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends a credential ID as the Cal.com user ID
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` constructs its request with `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, which is the Credential primary key rather than the owning user's ID. Credential and user IDs are unrelated, so the remote source will generally fail to find the user and can return credentials for another user whose ID happens to match the credential ID.

findings.title: Credential-sync refresh requests contain no authentication
findings.body: The configured credential-sync endpoint receives only a predictable user ID and app slug. The helper does not send `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` under `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`, nor any other authentication or signature, so an endpoint implemented according to this client cannot verify that a request came from its Cal.com instance. If that endpoint returns access tokens based on these fields, unauthenticated callers can request users' credentials.

findings.title: Credential sync cannot identify which credential to replace
findings.body: The payload identifies only a user and app, while the database permits multiple credentials for the same user and app (for example, the Google OAuth callback creates a credential on every connection). `findFirst` has no ordering and updates an arbitrary matching credential, leaving other stale credentials in place. Syncing one external account can therefore overwrite a different account's tokens and make bookings use the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Salesforce bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint
findings.body: Unlike the other modified integrations, Salesforce performs its refresh directly against Salesforce and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Consequently, when credential sharing is enabled, the configured source-of-truth endpoint is never queried for Salesforce and the implementation still depends on the locally stored refresh token.

findings.title: Salesforce creates its client with the stale access token after refreshing
findings.body: The new code obtains and persists `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, but the subsequent `jsforce.Connection` is initialized with `credentialKey.access_token`, the pre-refresh token. If that old token is expired—the condition that necessitates a refresh—the immediately returned client authenticates with the expired token rather than the token just received.

findings.title: Zoom sends a route name instead of its app slug to the sync endpoint
findings.body: This sends `zoomvideo` as `appSlug`, but the Zoom integration's installed app ID/slug is `zoom` (as used by `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts`). A source endpoint that keys credentials by the Cal.com app slug will not find Zoom credentials for this request, so Zoom token refresh fails only when syncing is enabled.
